When Cartier first sailed to Canada
column2: In 1535 Jacques Cartier made the first official French voyage to Canada, through the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

column1: When France founded its first permanent colony
column2: In 1605 the French founded Port Royal in Acadia (Nova Scotia), their first permanent colony in North America.

column1: How much a beaver hat cost in the 1610s
column2: As early as the 1610s a beaver hat sold for ten times the price of a wool hat, because Europeans had trapped their own beavers nearly to extinction.

column1: When the Iroquois destroyed the Hurons
column2: In 1648 and 1649 well-armed Iroquois warriors destroyed Huron towns, and the Hurons burned their remaining towns and abandoned their homeland for good.

column1: When La Salle reached the mouth of the Mississippi
column2: In 1682 La Salle became the first European to travel down the Mississippi to its mouth at the Gulf of Mexico.

column1: When epidemic devastated coastal New England
column2: From 1616 to 1618 a massive epidemic struck coastal New England, cutting the native population by as much as 90 percent.

column1: When and how many Pilgrims landed at Plymouth
column2: In November 1620 about 88 Separatist Pilgrims anchored at Plymouth, sick with scurvy and weak from malnutrition.

column1: When Winthrop founded Boston
column2: In 1630 John Winthrop's fleet arrived in Massachusetts Bay and founded Boston.

column1: How many came in the Great Migration
column2: About 21,000 Puritan immigrants came to New England between 1630 and 1642, until the English Civil War cut off arrivals.

column1: When the Salem witch trials took place
column2: In 1692 the Salem witchcraft trials led to twenty executions before Increase Mather and fourteen other ministers warned against them.

column1: When Metacom's War was fought
column2: Metacom's War (King Philip's War) was fought in 1675 and 1676, ending with Metacom's death in the summer of 1676.

column1: When the Dutch West India Company went bankrupt
column2: In 1654 the Dutch West India Company went bankrupt and virtually abandoned New Netherland.

column1: When the English took New Netherland
column2: In 1664 the Duke of York's invading fleet made the Dutch surrender New Netherland, which became New York.

column1: When William Penn received Pennsylvania
column2: In 1681 Charles II granted William Penn all the land between New Jersey and Maryland.

column1: When Parliament passed the first Navigation Act
column2: In 1651 Parliament passed the first Navigation Act; before it England had no coherent policy for regulating colonial trade.

column1: When the Dominion of New England was created
column2: In 1686 the Lords of Trade combined the New England colonies under a royal governor, and in 1688 they added New York and New Jersey.

column1: When the Glorious Revolution happened
column2: In 1688 Parliament forced James II into exile and made William and Mary monarchs in the Glorious Revolution.
